title: rec-c2.2-accepted-raw-seam
summary: The accepted-Raw seam. chronos-native persists a Raw record and returns its authoritative EventSeq; services subscribes an observer that derives durable TripwireFired evidence; the live fan-out happens last. dual_push is renamed accept_and_publish (the old name described the dual-write REC-C2 retires) and both spawn and attach go through the same seam. Closes FIND-C2.1-03 with a productive UAT: a real probe produces a real firing that survives restart with the same firing_seq/source_seq.

no_action: FIND-C2.2-02: FunctionName tripwire matching diverges between the raw matcher (TripwireCondition::matches(&TraceEvent), which requires TraceEvent.location.function) and the retired live semantic matcher (matching_semantic, which fell back to SemanticEvent.description). Surfaced by the C2.2.2 switchover: drain now reports the persisted firing count, so a FunctionName pattern can no longer match a ptrace syscall stream that carries no function location (m0_04 used to pass only because of the description fallback). This is a behaviour NARROWING, not a regression: tripwire_list's derived fire_count is durable too, so probe_drain and the tripwire view now agree instead of contradicting each other. m0_04 was rewritten to assert the canonical law (count == persisted evidence, invariant under a later subscription) and the narrowing is documented in the test. Whether FunctionName should also consider syscall names is a matcher-semantics decision that belongs to its own cycle, not to the drain switchover.

FIND-C2.2-03: 'partial' completeness status is now never produced by any reader (canonical_drain or events_read). Kept in the vocabulary deliberately for parity with C1; a future reader that can prove evidence loss inside the examined range is the intended owner.
